search_log.method: Read the complete chapter’s verse text and translations and recorded named individuals and explicit parentage/marriage relations only; the chapter synopsis and purports were excluded.

Read numbered verse text and translations for explicit spouse, teacher, appointment, and protection relations in the continuation involving Indra, Bṛhaspati, Brahmā and Viśvarūpa; the chapter synopsis and purports were excluded.

notes: Group labels and unnamed descendants are not person nodes: this excludes the 60,000 Paulomas/Kālakeyas as a group, the unnamed sons of several wives, the plural Aśvinī twins, and the unnamed demons/Devas. Named head Nivātakavaca is retained as a single son figure.
Translation variants explicitly presented as the same person are not split into duplicate nodes: Jayanta/Upendra, Skanda/Kārttikeya, and Anūru/Aruṇa each have one node.

Several same-name figures within this one chapter are deliberately kept distinct: Vibhāvasu (one of the Vasus) vs. Vibhāvasu (son of Danu); male Ariṣṭa vs. Dakṣa daughter Ariṣṭā; Danu’s son Aruṇa vs. Vinatā’s son Anūru/Aruṇa; male Danu’s son Pulomā vs. Vaiśvānara’s daughter Pulomā; and the two distinct women named Saṅkalpā and Saṅkalpa.

Claim evidence is the numbered Sanskrit verse and its verse translation only; contextual chapter summaries, editorial bracketed expansions, and purports are not treated as independent evidence. Where the translation expands Dharmarāja as Yamarāja in brackets, the claim is worded using the verse’s Dharmarāja designation and the existing Yama node.
